headline: Shiv Sena (UBT) Chief Uddhav Thackeray Hits Back At Union HM Amit Shah Over COVID-19 Remarks, Questions BJPs
content: Mumbai: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Tuesday hit back at Union Home Minister Amit Shah over his remarks that Thackeray had not answered his phone calls during the 2019-20 period when he was Maharashtra Chief Minister, asserting that the state's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic had earned national recognition despite the challenging circumstances.Thackeray said he had recently watched a video clip recalling Maharashtra's performance during the pandemic, when the state's then Chief Minister was counted among the country's best-performing CMs. He said he had always credited the entire government machinery rather than claiming individual credit for the achievement.Uddhav Thackeray Defends Maharashtra's COVID-19 ResponseTaking a dig at Shah, Thackeray said there was little point in explaining the state's performance to people who were unwilling to understand facts.Countering Shah's claim about unanswered phone calls, the Sena (UBT) chief said the situation in Maharashtra would have resembled the scenes witnessed in Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat during the pandemic had the state's administration failed to respond effectively. He pointed out that bodies were found floating in the Ganga in Uttar Pradesh, while funeral pyres were seen burning in public places in Gujarat.Whether it was Dharavi or other parts of Maharashtra, the entire government machinery had worked effectively, he said, adding that Maharashtra had demonstrated through its work what could not be achieved merely by the Prime Minister asking people to bang plates during the pandemic.Questions Amit Shah Over Oxygen-Related Deaths In Uttar PradeshThackeray also questioned Shah over the deaths of 70 children due to a shortage of oxygen at a hospital in Uttar Pradesh, asking whether the Union Home Minister had intervened or contacted the then Chief Minister to ensure oxygen supplies. He said the BJP leadership should explain why it had failed to demonstrate the same concern at the time.In another attack, Thackeray criticised Shah for praising late NCP leader Ajit Pawar, saying the BJP had earlier made Pawar's life miserable by accusing him of involvement in an alleged Rs 70,000-crore corruption scam.Demands Apology Over Earlier Corruption AllegationsReferring to Shah's remarks at the unveiling of Ajit Pawar's bust at the Pune Zilla Parishad office on Monday, Thackeray said the appreciation would have meant something had it come when Pawar was alive. He said Shah should apologise to Pawar and acknowledge that the allegations were untrue.Navi Mumbai: Police Bust Alleged Ayurvedic Product Investment Racket With 9,000 IDs, Arrest Company CMD And 3 AgentsThe former Chief Minister also demanded that Shah visit violence-hit Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh, where he alleged people were confronting Chinese incursions alongside security forces. He further accused the BJP of treating governance and administration as secondary concerns.Targeting the Centre over its handling of protests against the NEET paper leak, Thackeray said Shah had failed to appear in Parliament to respond to the Opposition's allegations regarding police action against Gen Z protesters.With Assembly elections approaching in Uttar Pradesh, Thackeray said voters should not forget the hardships they faced during the COVID-19 pandemic. headline: UK’s House of Commons Passes Controversial Immigration Bill
content: (Bloomberg) -- Labour’s controversial immigration reforms passed through the House of Commons, avoiding a major backbench rebellion in a relief for Prime Minister Andy Burnham.The Immigration and Asylum Bill was approved on Tuesday by a 290-94 vote. It will now pass to the House of Lords, the UK’s second legislative chamber, for further scrutiny. The legislation had threatened to cause a headache for Burnham and his Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, as several Labour MPs expressed concern about provisions making it harder for migrants already in the country to claim settled status. The reforms would extend the baseline time over which a migrant must live in the country to 10 years from five, with that timeline shortened for the well-paid and lengthened for refugees.After more than 100 MPs wrote to Mahmood threatening to vote against the bill, and under the new premiership of the more left-leaning Burnham, Mahmood agreed to a carve-out for migrants who’d come to work in low-paid social care jobs looking after the UK’s elderly and vulnerable. The home secretary conceded earlier this month that they could stay on a five-year path, as long as they arrived before May 2025 — when she first outlined her proposals — and that their earnings in the 12 months prior to their application should be at least £25,000 ($33,000). Under the original plan, they had faced an extension to 15 years. But other skilled workers earning less than £50,270 — including chefs and engineers — are still facing longer pathways to settlement. Some MPs remain uneasy about the government’s plans to make retroactive changes that potentially add years onto the settlement timeline for people who may have been just weeks away from being able to gain settled status.An amendment tabled by Labour backbencher Neil Duncan-Jordan, which would have prevented the government changing immigration rules for people already in the UK on a skilled worker visa, received 44 votes. Speaking ahead of the vote on behalf of the government, Border Security and Asylum Minister Anna Turley said: “I profoundly disagree with the word restrospection” when used to describe the way the reforms applied to migrants already in the country.“Settlement has always been determined at the point of application, not at entry,” she said. People should not “have a sense of entitlement” to institutions like the UK’s schools and National Health Service when they come to the country, she added.Mahmood has been keen to change the immigration rules after hundreds of thousands of people arrived to work in the UK following Brexit and the subsequent relaxation of work visa eligibility. Gaining settled status would allow workers whose visas had been tied to a particular job to work in any other industry, and to claim a wider range of benefits.The Home Office was concerned that this could add to the UK’s already ballooning welfare bill. Under its proposals, the government said, around 500,000 people will now have to wait longer to claim settled status than they otherwise would. headline: AAP presses Centre to reopen Kartarpur Corridor before Guru Nanak Parkash Purab
content: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Punjab has urged the BJP-led Central Government to reopen the Sri Kartarpur Sahib Corridor ahead of the 557th Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji, citing the religious sentiments of Sikh devotees awaiting access to the shrine. The demand was raised on Monday by party MP Malvinder Singh Kang and chief spokesperson Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal, who questioned the Centre’s decision to keep the corridor closed.Kang said Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann had already written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, conveying the concerns of the global Sikh community and seeking the corridor’s immediate reopening. The party said the continued closure was affecting devotees who wished to pay obeisance at the historic shrine.Appeal ahead of Parkash PurabKang said Sri Kartarpur Sahib had immense religious and historical significance as the place where Guru Nanak Dev Ji spent a considerable part of his life and shared the message of “Kirat Karo”. With the 557th Parkash Purab approaching, he urged the Prime Minister to ensure that the corridor was reopened in time for devotees to visit the shrine.He said the sentiments of the Sikh community across the world should be respected and that the Centre should act without further delay. The party’s appeal comes ahead of the annual observance, when devotees seek an opportunity to visit the place associated with the founder of Sikhism.Dhaliwal, speaking at Dera Baba Nanak, said Sikh devotees gathered on the 15th of every month to pray for the reopening of the corridor. He described it as unfortunate that their repeated prayers and appeals had not resulted in access being restored.Security rationale questionedDhaliwal questioned the Centre’s stated security concerns, asking why trade with Pakistan could continue through other routes, including Gujarat’s ports, while pilgrims remained unable to travel to Kartarpur Sahib. He said the government should explain the distinction between allowing commercial activity and restricting religious visits.The AAP leader alleged that the continued closure was political rather than solely a security-related decision. He accused the BJP-led government of discriminating against Punjab and the Sikh community, and said religious sentiments should not be affected by political considerations.Dhaliwal also referred to businesses linked to industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani while questioning why commercial links with Pakistan could continue through routes connected to Gujarat’s ports. These remarks were part of his criticism of the Centre’s position on the corridor.The AAP leaders called for the gates to be reopened before the 557th Parkash Purab, arguing that devotees should be able to pay obeisance at Sri Kartarpur Sahib and seek the blessings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. The party said the shrine held a special place in Sikh history and that access to it remained an important concern for the community.

headline: J&K Assembly panel raises concerns over Jammu’s civic deficiencies
content: The Committee on Environment of the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly on Monday conducted an on-the-spot inspection of various areas in the city to assess environmental concerns and civic infrastructure deficiencies, particularly those related to sewerage management, drinking water supply and sanitation.Headed by CPM MLA MY Tarigami, the Committee started its tour with a visit to the Mubarak Mandi Heritage Complex and adjoining localities of the old city, with one of its members and National Conference legislator Salman Sagar calling for a detailed examination of the shortcomings in the smart city projects and fixing accountability.Talking to reporters, Tarigami said the committee was constituted under the mandate of the Legislative Assembly to examine environmental issues and work toward improving citizens' quality of life.The objective was to ensure that people have access to clean air, safe drinking water, better sanitation and properly maintained streets, emphasising that environmental concerns should remain above political considerations," he said."We have also noticed garbage dumps at several places in Jammu, just as there are similar issues in Srinagar. This is not about politics. Whether it is the previous government or the present one, our common objective should be to ensure that Mubarak Mandi and the entire city of Jammu remain clean and beautiful," Tarigami said.Stressing the importance of environmental protection, he called for collective efforts by the government, administration, elected representatives and citizens to address civic problems.Sagar said the committee's objective was to bring elected representatives and senior government officers together to address public issues, but ground realities in several localities presented a concerning picture.Referring to the condition of Mubarak Mandi and its adjoining areas, he said residents had complained that little had changed since 2007, with dilapidated streets and bylanes, inadequate sewage management and problems in drinking water supply.He said residents had also raised concerns about sewage and drinking water allegedly mixing due to leakages in pipelines, calling for urgent intervention to address these basic infrastructure deficiencies.Despite the implementation of the Smart City project, Sagar said several fundamental civic issues remained unresolved."We need to examine the shortcomings in the Smart City projects - why they occurred, how they happened, who was responsible, where the problems arose and what the reasons were," he said, stressing the need to fix accountability and undertake corrective measures.

headline: Mandi-Jaunapur Road may come under NHAI to ease south Delhi traffic
content: New Delhi: The Centre has initiated the process of considering the Mandi-Jaunapur Road in south Delhi for inclusion in its new highway development programme, a move that could help ease chronic traffic congestion in the area.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari informed South Delhi MP Ramvir Singh Bidhuri about the development in a letter, following the latter’s repeated requests to bring the road under National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).In the letter, Gadkari said officials had been directed to examine the proposal, keeping in view the need for highway infrastructure development in the South Delhi parliamentary constituency. He, however, noted that roads have to meet the prescribed criteria before they can be brought under NHAI’s ambit.Bidhuri had raised the issue in Lok Sabha, arguing that the Mandi-Jaunapur Road was a major traffic bottleneck in south Delhi. He pointed out that the Faridabad-Gurgaon Road and Mehrauli-Gurgaon Road, both of which witness heavy traffic, have already been taken over by NHAI, while the Mandi-Jaunapur Road, which links the two corridors, continues to face severe congestion.According to Bidhuri, the stretch is designated as a 200-foot-wide master plan road, but its actual width at several places is only around 30 feet. headline: Gadkari seeks detailed reports of five road projects in Panipat | Hindustan Times
content: The Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari directed highway officials to initiate the preparation of detailed project reports (DPRs) for five major road projects in Panipat.The proposals were submitted by the education minister Mahipal Dhanda during his meeting with Gadkari in New Delhi, highlighting the ever-increasing traffic pressure in the industrial and commercial town on the Delhi-Chandigarh highway.The projects include expanding road and flyover infrastructure to relieve city residents from traffic jams and boost the industrial economy.  One of the five major projects is a proposal for constructing a ring road for Panipat. Neighbouring Karnal and Ambala already have ring roads, which are likely to be operational by next year.Dhanda said the road will ease growing traffic congestion in Panipat city and allow heavy vehicles to travel from outside without entering the city.Construction of two new flyovers from Sector-13-17 flyover to Babarpur flyover and another in front of Babarpur mandi has been sought. A demand for an underpass in front of Eldeco, a residential society on the outskirts, was also presented to the union minister.“Given the traffic pressure in front of Babarpur Mandi, a demand was made for a new flyover. This will facilitate the movement of farmers, traders, and common citizens traveling to and from the market area and improve the traffic system,” Dhanda said.A proposal was also made for an entry ramp on the GT Road flyover in Panipat city and an exit ramp in front of Nathu Sweets on the other side, saving commuters time.The Haryana minister also sought the construction of access roads on both sides for Panipat Grain Market for the convenience of farmers, commission agents, and traders.

headline: Punjab and Haryana high court grants bail to ponzi scheme accused | Hindustan Times
content: The Punjab and Haryana high court has granted bail in a money laundering case to the alleged kingpin of a ponzi scheme, in which around 80,000 persons were allegedly duped of crores of rupees.“The seriousness of the allegations, though an important consideration, cannot be the sole ground for keeping an accused in custody for an indefinite period, particularly when the investigation has been completed,” the bench of justice Sumeet Goel said while granting bail to one Harinder Pal Singh.The Enforcement Directorate (ED) had initiated investigation in February 2024 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002. The probe stems from an FIR filed by the Himachal Police in October 2023 on a complaint alleging a fraud of ₹12 lakh on the pretext of investment in Forex promising high returns. Subsequently, the number of criminal cases went up to seven FIRs, including one in Panchkula. At one point, the investigators had estimated it to be a fraud of ₹210 crore.The petitioner, a government schoolteacher in Punjab, had claimed that he was falsely implicated in the case and his name did not figure in the initial FIR registered in Mandi district of Himachal Pradesh. He claimed that he was later named by the ED on the basis of statements by some accused persons. He was arrested in September 2025.His counsel, senior advocate Bipan Ghai, had argued that Harinder should be granted bail as the investigation was complete. Ghai also pointed out that the ED had cited 49 prosecution witnesses and the challan filed in the case ran into more than 12,400 pages.On the other hand, the ED had claimed that allegations were serious in nature and related to a large-scale organised investment fraud involving thousands of innocent investors. The ED had termed him one of the key accused in the fraud.The court said that the allegations regarding the diversion of funds through different entities, generation of proceeds of crime and acquisition of properties in India and abroad, were matters that would require proper examination/adjudication during the course of trial.It added that nothing had been brought on record to indicate that any further custodial interrogation of the petitioner was either required or contemplated.“The petitioner cannot be expected to remain incarcerated for an indefinite period merely because the allegations relate to an economic offence. Thus, the prolonged incarceration, coupled with the absence of a reasonable possibility of the trial concluding within a foreseeable period, cannot be ignored while considering a prayer for bail,” it said while granting him bail.

headline: MCC, Devaraja Market traders to continue talks on rent hike
content: MYSURU A meeting convened to discuss the revision of rents for shops in the century-old Devaraja Market and other markets under the control of Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) was held at the corporation office on Tuesday. The meeting was organised following objections from traders to the revised rents, with the MCC seeking to address their concerns and arrive at a consensus. Besides the Devaraja Market, the corporation also manages markets in Mandi Mohalla. Chaired by MLA K. Harish Gowda, the meeting focused on the rent revision at the Devaraja Market. Responding to the objections raised by traders, Mr. Gowda reportedly maintained that the rent hike was “reasonable”, considering the increase in maintenance costs and other expenses incurred by the corporation. Several traders have not accepted the revised rents, which came into effect in May 2026 under a new scheme. However, a section of traders is understood to have agreed to the revision, pointing out that rents were being revised after a gap of several years. Devaraja Market, a century-old heritage structure, houses more than 600 shops. MCC Commissioner M.K. Savita was present. Another meeting has been scheduled for November 23. Traders are expected to hold discussions among themselves and arrive at a common stand before the next meeting with the officials.

headline: NDMC nod to Rs 54-crore solar expansion, 40 smart toilets, Rs 106 crore for drain cleaning
content: Rs 54 crore rooftop solar expansion project, Rs 106 crore for desilting drains, construction of five Prakriti cafes, offering “wholesome food options”, and 40 smart public toilets — these are among the major civic infrastructure initiatives approved by the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) on Tuesday. The decisions were taken at a council meeting chaired by Deputy Chief Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh and attended by New Delhi MP Bansuri Swaraj, NDMC Chairperson Manoj Kumar Dwivedi, and Vice-Chairperson Kuljeet Singh Chahal, officials said. As part of its renewable energy push, the council granted administrative approval for a rooftop solar project expansion. A survey conducted by The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) across 244 NDMC buildings identified an additional solar potential of 6,914 kilowatts . Of these, 40 buildings have been recommended for implementation under the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) model, while the remaining 204 will follow the capital expenditure (CAPEX) model. Another survey of 124 non-NDMC buildings identified a further solar potential of 8.25 Megawatts. Tenders for these projects will be floated through an Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI). The total projected cost for this rooftop solar initiative is Rs 54 crore over a tenure of 25 years, officials said. According to officials, discussions are also underway with Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs), market associations, and government institutions to expand rooftop solar coverage. Further, NDMC will also construct more than 40 smart public toilets at locations including Khan Market, Janpath, Chanakyapuri, Malcha Marg, Mandi House, Connaught Place and Hanuman Mandir. The facilities will have touch-free sensors, ventilation systems and AI-enabled daily maintenance monitoring, an official said. Three dedicated Pink Toilets for women are also planned. On the new toilets set to be constructed, Chahal said, “Past non-performing agencies, such as in Khan Market, were terminated and litigated up to the High Court. New contracts explicitly disqualify past defaulters, hold NDMC accountable, and mandate daily AI-driven digital maintenance checks.” The council has also approved the establishment of five eco-friendly Prakriti Cafes at Lodhi Garden, Nehru Park and BRICS Garden under the Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) model. Under the model, the selected agency will develop the cafes at its own cost and undertake their operation and maintenance before transferring them to NDMC in accordance with the prescribed terms and conditions. Officials also said that Rs 106 crore has been allocated for desilting 14 major drainage networks across the NDMC area. The exercise will cover both conventional drains and old British-era brick barrel drainage lines, with chief engineers assigned operational zones to oversee the work and ensure that the network is cleared before the monsoon, they added. The council also discussed changes to property tax assessment, with NDMC proposing to introduce the Unit Area Method (UAM) in line with the 'One City, One Tax' principle. A stakeholder consultation on the proposed system is scheduled for November 23. Among other decisions, NDMC also sanctioned Rs 40 crore for security services at its offices, markets, and parking facilities and approved revised recruitment regulations for technical posts in its Electricity department. The council further said that tenders had been floated for addressing 700 dark spots across the NDMC area, with the project targeted for completion by June 2027.

headline: NHA estimates show rising out-of-pocket expenditure, declining government spending on health in Keralam
content: Thiruvananthapuram The just-released National Health Accounts 2023-24 has no surprises for Kerala, which continues to top the charts as far as the out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) on health is concerned, with households in the State putting in nearly two-thirds of the State’s total health expenditure from their own pockets. The estimates for 2023-24, released by the National Health Systems Resource Centre, Union Health Ministry, shows that the State has the highest annual per capita OOPE on health in the country, at ₹8,870, against a national average of ₹2,901. Of the State’s total health expenditure of ₹48,979 crore in 2023-24, ₹31,931 crore were people’s own spending. OOPE, as a proportion of the total health expenditure went up from 59.1% in 2021-22 to 65.2% in 2023-24. But the worrisome trend is that, alongside the rising total expenditure on health in the State and the OOPE on health, the government spending on health in Keralam has been on the decline since 2021-22. Whatever increase occurred in the State’s health bill is being borne by households and not the government. The proportion of government health expenditure, as a part of the total health expenditure of the State fell from 32.7% in 2021-22 to 25% in 2023-24. In absolute amount, this is a drop from ₹15,618 crore in 2021-22 to ₹12,226 crore in 2023-24. Per capita expenses The per capita health expenditure in Keralam is ₹13,605. However, the per capita government spending on health or the public spending on health per person fell from ₹4,338 in 2021-22 to ₹3,396 in 2023-24. In 2021-22, if Kerala spent about 5.2% of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) on health, in 2023-24, this declined to 4.3%, (even though the State actually spent ₹945 crores more on health in 2023-24 in terms of absolute amount) When compared to 2022-23 also, the latest NHA reports show a rise in total health expenditure by 3.7% and an increase in OOPE by 5.7%, while the government’s health expenditure declined by 5.5%. At the national level At the same time, compared to the previous year, at the national level, national per capita government expenditure on health shows a slight increase in 23-24 at ₹2,959 while the OOPE on health correspondingly showed a slight decline to touch ₹2,767. Kerala’s per capita government spending on health was 37% above the national average in 2021-22. But this edge has narrowed to 15% in the 2023-24 estimates, with the per capita government health expenditure at ₹3,396. Fourth in India Kerala now ranks fourth among the 21 States in the NHA report as far as per capita government spending on health is concerned, behind Himachal Pradesh (₹5,171), Uttarakhand (₹4,142) and Odisha (₹3,718) It is perhaps unfair to compare Kerala with the rest of the country, given the State’s unique profile, with its increasing morbidities of lifestyle diseases, a rapidly ageing population, high health-seeking behaviour of people and an overwhelming reliance on private health care. However, the 'fall' in government spending on health in the State would need to be examined more carefully. Kerala has been focussing on improving primary care facilities and over the last 10 years, substantial investment has gone into the improvement of health infrastructure in the public sector, especially in the secondary and tertiary care levels. However, the public continues to rely largely on the private sector for care, which would naturally increase the OOPE on health The growing burden of lifestyle diseases and the cost of treating the complications of chronic illnesses is one of the primary reasons for the high cost of care. Outpatient expenses, drugs and diagnostics constitute a chunk of the OOPE on health in Kerala and none of this is covered by health insurance schemes.

headline: Sonia’s memoir ‘Belonging’ debuts with 2 lakh copies sold in under a week: HarperCollins India CEO
content: New Delhi From dominating headlines since its announcement in August to flying off bookstore shelves, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir has had a blockbuster run, with HarperCollins India CEO Ananth Padmanabhan saying it has sold “over two lakh copies” in less than a week, broken multiple publishing records and emerged as one of the “biggest memoirs” in independent India’s history. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/indian-national-congress/ Sonia Gandhi’s ‘Belonging’: From being shelved to the shelves Sonia Gandhi’s ‘Belonging’: From being shelved to the shelves Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, “Belonging: A Journey of Love,” is set for release on November 10, with HarperCollins India handling its publication domestically. Sonia Gandhi’s ‘Belonging’: From being shelved to the shelves seriespackage 1 “Belonging: A Journey of Love”, officially launched at a packed event at ITC Maurya in New Delhi on Monday (November 16, 2026), was attended by the who’s who of the Congress and the INDIA opposition bloc, literary figures and a host of Chief Ministers, including Tamil Nadu’s C. Joseph Vijay, Karnataka’s D.K. Shivakumar and Himachal Pradesh’s Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. Celebrating the book’s unprecedented sales, Mr. Padmanabhan said it has already set several publishing records — and clearly not one at a time — with more than two lakh copies sold in less than a week after going on sale at 10 a.m. last Tuesday (November 10, 2026). “With more than two lakh copies sold in less than a week, the book has broken many records already: it is the fastest-selling book, the fastest-selling debut, the fastest-selling work of non-fiction and the fastest-selling memoir,” he said. More than “15,000 copies” were also delivered in under 10 minutes on the day of publication, making it the fastest-delivered book in the country’s publishing history, he added. According to industry insiders, while the benchmark for declaring a book a bestseller varies depending on the author, genre and publisher, a title in India is generally considered a bestseller once it crosses the 10,000-copy mark. Review | Sonia Gandhi’s Belonging: A memoir of revelation and reticence Review | Sonia Gandhi’s Belonging: A memoir of revelation and reticence The memoir stands out for its striking candour, not as much for its scrutiny of the party and its leadership Review | Sonia Gandhi’s Belonging: A memoir of revelation and reticence storyline 1 The thunderous response to the book has clearly taken even the debut author by surprise, with Ms. Gandhi admitting that she is “overwhelmed” by the outpouring of love and affection from readers. “I always thought people would be impressed within certain weeks, but this has been overwhelming, unexpected and overwhelming,” Ms. Gandhi said. “I am deeply touched by the love and affection people have shown in their comments, in buying the book and even in the critiques. Those are the reasons,” the Congress Parliamentary Party chief said with a smile, drawing thunderous applause from the packed hall, including from her children — Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and AICC general secretary Priyanka Gandhi. Initially slated to be published in India by Penguin Random House, the memoir found a new publisher, HarperCollins India, after the author and the former publishing house failed to reach an agreement over certain editorial changes. While Congress leaders alleged pressure to remove politically-sensitive references, Penguin denied any external interference, maintaining that the disagreement was part of its regular editorial process. With the book now breaking sales records, Mr. Padmanabhan and the team at HarperCollins India are clearly laughing all the way to the bank. However, Padmanabhan remained tight-lipped about how HarperCollins India came on board, saying it is a “story for another day”. He did reveal, though, that the publishing house had “less than 12 weeks” to bring the book to readers. And the effort appears to have paid off handsomely. In a lighter moment, Mr. Padmanabhan quipped that there are now only three kinds of people in India — “those who bought the book and read it, those who bought the book and are waiting for it to be delivered and those who bought the book, read it, but do not have the courage to admit it.” “Belonging: A Journey of Love” is a personal memoir, with politics providing the background or “a kind of framework”, as Gandhi writes in the book.

headline: States to spend Rs 4 lakh crore in FY27 on unconditional cash transfers
content: Indian states are likely to spend Rs 4 lakh crore on unconditional cash transfers in the current fiscal, more than double what was spent in 2022-23. Equal to 1% of the country’s GDP, the money spent on such transfers rose by 24% every year from 2018-19 to 2023-24. This was twice the growth seen in subsidies, with the 16th Finance Commission noting that states that have increased their expenditure on unconditional transfers “also tended to be those with a revenue deficit”. The above figures are based on an analysis by New Delhi-based think-tank PRS Legislative Research of 128 such cash transfer schemes for women, farmers, youth, and social security pension beneficiaries. According to PRS, the list is not exhaustive, and therefore, the actual expenditure by states on such initiatives could be higher. “In seven states, unconditional transfers account for more than half of the total expenditure on subsidies and transfers,” PRS said in a report on Tuesday, noting that these states include the likes of West Bengal (61%) and Assam (60%). More broadly, PRS said 52% of states’ revenue receipts in 2026-27 are to be spent on things that can’t be postponed: salaries, pensions, and interest on borrowings. Backing for cash transfers Unconditional cash transfers and similar schemes aimed at women – PRS estimates nearly 90% of cash transfers are towards women and social security pensions – have become increasingly popular at the state level, especially in the run up to elections. And while they are seen as adding to states’ fiscal burden – for seven states, these transfers make up more than half of their total expenditure on subsidies and transfers – they are also praised for increasing public welfare. In July, a paper by the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) analysed account-level monthly data to evaluate Maharashtra’s Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana and Odisha’s Subhadra Yojana and found the schemes boosted expenditure by as much as 46% in the case of Maharashtra and 28% for Odisha. The paper went on to argue that noy only should both the scheme be continued, but their amounts should be periodically reviewed to adjust for inflation and household spending patterns. Maharashtra’s Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana involves the monthly transfer of Rs 1,500 to eligible women, while the Subhadra Yojana scheme offers biannual instalments totalling Rs 10,000 per year. More broadly, economists highlight the positive impact of even small targeted and unconditional cash transfers to women, arguing that they offer protection from shocks such as diseases and help better the well-being of households, improve food security, contribute to the education of children, and promote savings. Other schemes, which have been termed ‘freebies’ by some and criticised, include the likes of free bus travel for women. However, the statistics ministry’s first-ever household travel survey, released last month, seemingly backed the decision by several states to offer free bus travel to women, with more than a fifth of urban women using this mode of transport to go to work, three times as high as urban men. In some states, the fraction of urban women commuting to work by bus was significantly higher than the national average: 46.8% in Keralam, 41.1% in Tamil Nadu, 34.9% in Karnataka, and 28.9% in Telangana. Experts say participation of women in the labour force is closely linked to access to affordable public transport. The debt problem However, elevated debt levels at the Centre and state levels – often referred together as general government debt – have been repeatedly cited by global ratings agencies as a key weakness of India’s public finances. In January, the Reserve Bank of India had called on state governments to target a reduction in their debt levels, like the Centre. It said that while social welfare programmes are essential in a country such as India where economic disparities remain stark, “these welfare expenditures run the risk of crowding out critical investments in physical and social infrastructure”. According to PRS, outstanding liabilities of four states crossed 40% of their Gross State Domestic Product in 2025-26: Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Nagaland, and Punjab. Most states, it said, have not been able to reduce their debt levels significantly. The Centre is targeting a reduction in its debt-to-GDP ratio to 49-51% by March 2031 from 56.1% in 2025-26. Meanwhile, the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Review Committee of 2017 had recommended a maximum debt-to-GDP ratio of 20% for states by 2023. As of March, this figure was around 28%, with PRS noting that only three states – Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Odisha – estimate their debt to be under 20%.

headline: Himachal Pradesh government to refund Rs 4.27 crore application fees to candidates who applied for 80 pos
content: The Himachal Pradesh government will refund Rs 4.27 crore collected as application fees from candidates who applied for recruitment examinations under 80 post codes of the erstwhile Himachal Pradesh Staff Selection Commission (HPSSC), Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu informed the state Assembly on Monday.The announcement covers 1,43,435 candidates who had submitted applications for the examinations conducted through the former recruitment commission. The refund decision was communicated through a written reply to a joint question raised by BJP MLAs Sudhir Sharma and Vipin Singh Parmar during the winter session of the Himachal Pradesh Assembly.According to the chief minister's response, the government had collected Rs 4.27 crore in application fees from applicants across the 80 post codes. The proposed refund will return the amount collected from candidates whose recruitment processes were affected following the dissolution of the commission.Rs 4.27 crore collected from 1.43 lakh applicantsThe figures shared by the chief minister indicate the scale of applications received for recruitment examinations under the former HPSSC. A total of 1,43,435 candidates had applied for posts advertised under 80 different post codes, generating application fee collections of Rs 4.27 crore.Post codes refer to separate recruitment categories for different government positions. The government also clarified that there is currently no proposal under consideration to revise the existing application fee structure.The announcement comes amid continuing efforts by the state government to restructure its recruitment mechanism following the controversy surrounding the former selection commission.HPSSC dissolved after question paper leak caseThe Himachal Pradesh Staff Selection Commission was dissolved in February 2023 after a question paper leak came to light on December 23, 2022. The case emerged after the state vigilance bureau arrested Uma Azad, a senior assistant at the commission, and allegedly recovered a solved question paper and Rs 2.5 lakh in cash from her possession.The incident raised questions about the integrity of the recruitment process and prompted the state government to discontinue the commission's functioning.In September 2023, the government established the Rajya Chayan Aayog, or State Selection Commission, to take over recruitment-related responsibilities and replace the erstwhile HPSSC.State Selection Commission expands online examination infrastructureResponding to the Assembly question, Sukhu also outlined the steps being taken to strengthen the examination infrastructure under the newly established State Selection Commission.The examination agency engaged by the commission has established 41 examination centres across almost all districts of Himachal Pradesh to facilitate the conduct of computer-based examinations.The commission is also working to establish additional computer-based testing centres in every district. The objective, according to the chief minister, is to reduce the distance candidates need to travel to appear for recruitment examinations.The expansion of examination infrastructure is expected to improve access to online recruitment tests, particularly for candidates residing in remote and geographically difficult areas of the hill state.17 recruitment requisitions pending with commissionThe chief minister further informed the Assembly that the State Selection Commission currently has 17 recruitment requisitions pending from various government departments.Advertisements for the posts covered under these requisitions are yet to be issued. The pending requisitions indicate the recruitment workload awaiting processing through the restructured selection mechanism.The government has not provided a timeline for the release of advertisements for these posts in the written response.Patwari recruitment receives over 1.87 lakh applicationsSeparately, the chief minister shared figures related to the recruitment of Patwaris in the state. The recruitment process received 1,87,257 applications, while the application fees collected amounted to Rs 14.98 crore.The figures provide an indication of the volume of applications received for government recruitment in Himachal Pradesh.The disclosure of the Rs 4.27 crore refund decision, along with details of pending recruitment requisitions and examination infrastructure, places the state's recruitment process back in focus as the government works through the transition from the former HPSSC to the Rajya Chayan Aayog.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. headline: STPI IT Export Awards - 2026
content: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), established by the Government of India under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology in 1991, with a prime objective to promote and boost the Software and Electronic Hardware exports from the country. STPI has a presence across 73 locations in the country. Within the Karnataka jurisdiction, the main centre is located in Bengaluru, supported by sub-centres in Mysuru, Hubballi, Mangaluru, Manipal, and Davanagere. For over three decades, STPI has played a regulatory role in promoting software and electronic hardware exports from India. It has been proactively involved in creating a supportive ecosystem for the IT/ITES/ESDM Industry, with the aim of enabling the sector to realize its full potential and contribute significantly to the Nation’s economic growth. STPI has been a key growth driver for the Indian Information Technology and Electronic Hardware industries over the past three decades. By implementing Government of India Schemes, Policies and Incentives by providing robust infrastructure support such as high-quality Data communication services, Data center services, Cloud services and incubation facilities. STPI has significantly contributed to nurturing Industry growth. Its dual role as an industry promoter and service provider has been an essential element in the success of India’s IT offshore sector. STPI Bengaluru has largest number of IT/ITES/ESDM exporting companies. The IT/ITES/ESDM Exports from Karnataka have seen remarkable growth from Rs 5.6 crore in 1991-92 to Rs. 5.43 lakh crores in 2025-26.The growth is around 16 % compared to the previous year exports of 4.68 lakh crore, which contributes 43% to the National Exports under STPI. The STP/EHTP units in Karnataka collectively provide direct employment to 11.66 lakh professionals. At present, 1,800+ IT/ITES companies and 32 electronic hardware companies are registered under the STPI umbrella in the Bengaluru jurisdiction. Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 is India’s flagship annual International IT & BT event, organized by the Department of Electronics, IT, BT & S&T, Government of Karnataka, since 1998. STPI has been a co-host of this prestigious event since its inception, contributing to its growth and global reach over the past 28 years. The 29th edition of BTS-2026 under the theme ‘AI & Beyond’ is being held at the Bengaluru International Exhibition Centre (BIEC), Tumkur Road, Bengaluru, from 17th to 19th November 2026. Over the years, the STPI IT Export Awards have become one of the most prestigious recognitions for the IT/ITES/ESDM industry in Karnataka.

headline: NEEPCO Organises Mizoram State-Level Painting Competition on Energy Conservation 2026; 100 Students Shortlisted from 2,448 Participants

Khogendra Meitei, General Manager (HR), NEEPCO, also attended the programme, along with representatives of NEEPCO, jury members, participating students, parents and media personnel. headline: Master Trainers’ Training Programme for Second Phase of Census 2027 Begins in Guwahati
content: The four-day residential Master Trainers’ Training Programme for the second phase of Census 2027, covering Population Enumeration (PE), commenced today at the Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE), Lalmati, Guwahati. The training programme will continue from 17 to 20 November 2026. A total of 66 Master Trainers are participating in the programme, including 50 officials from various districts of Assam and 16 officials from the Directorate of Census Operations (DCO), Assam. The programme aims to prepare a trained pool of Master Trainers who will further impart training to Field Trainers for the smooth and effective conduct of Census 2027 across the State. The inaugural session was attended by Shri Biswajit Pegu, IAS, Director-cum-Chief Principal Census Officer, Assam; Shri Partha Pegu, ACS, State Government Nodal Officer for Census 2027 and Additional Secretary, General Administration Department, Government of Assam; and Shri A.S.S. Dewan, Faculty Member, IIE. Addressing the participants, the dignitaries highlighted the importance of Census 2027 in supporting evidence-based planning, policy formulation and effective governance. They also emphasised the responsibility of Master Trainers in ensuring proper training of field functionaries and maintaining accuracy and quality in the collection of census data. The technical sessions on the first day covered various aspects of Population Enumeration, including census concepts, procedures, schedules, field-level protocols and the use of digital tools and applications developed for Census 2027. The sessions also included interactive discussions and practical demonstrations to familiarise participants with their roles and responsibilities. The training is being conducted by four National Trainers: Shri Bikash Nath, Joint Director-cum-Joint Chief Principal Census Officer, Assam; Shri Paragjyoti Borkakoty, Deputy Director-cum-Deputy Chief Principal Census Officer, Assam; Shri Pragyan Jyoti Khound, Deputy Director-cum-Deputy Chief Principal Census Officer, Assam; and Shri Nayan Moni Gogoi, Deputy Director-cum-Deputy Chief Principal Census Officer, Assam.

headline: Former sarpanch dies after poll-related clash in Rajasthan’s Jhunjhunu; villagers block road
content: A former sarpanch died after being injured in a clash during panchayat polls in Rajasthan's Jhunjhunu district, triggering protests on Tuesday as thousands of villagers blocked a road demanding the arrest of those involved, officials said.The protesters gathered near Karmadi village and blocked the Khetri-Jaipur road, disrupting traffic.The deceased, identified as former sarpanch Laxminarayan Saini, was seriously injured in a scuffle outside a polling station in Vijaynagar gram panchayat on Monday. The clash reportedly took place at a booth set up outside the polling station for preparing voter slips.Saini was referred to Jaipur for treatment but died on the way, after which his body was kept at the mortuary in Neem Ka Thana, according to the information available.His daughter-in-law is contesting the sarpanch election, the report said.The incident triggered tension in the area, with villagers demanding the immediate arrest of the accused. A large police force has been deployed in Vijaynagar, while police and administrative officials are monitoring the situation.The protesters remained on the road, insisting that action be taken against those involved in the clash.

headline: Why is Telangana merging its Board of Intermediate Education with Department of School Education? | Explained
content: HYDERABAD Telangana plans to integrate Intermediate education into the school system from the 2027–28 academic year, bringing Classes 11 and 12 under a unified framework. Chief Minister A. This ends a 55-year-old administrative separation between schools and junior colleges.

headline: 'Testicular surgery on female patient under HIMCARE': Himachal CM alleges irregularities in scheme
content: Shimla/Dharamshala: An investigation into the HIMCARE scheme has uncovered a record of "testicular surgery performed on a female patient", Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu claimed in the Assembly on Tuesday, alleging irregularities in the programme launched by the previous BJP government. .Sukhu stated this while intervening during a discussion on an adjournment motion moved in the House by the opposition BJP on the issue of corruption. .Hitting back, Leader of Opposition (LoP) Jai Ram Thakur, in a statement, alleged that CM Sukhu was repeatedly making "false and shameful statements" to discredit the HIMCARE scheme as he has failed to achieve any significant milestone during his four-year tenure. .'You see news and file PIL': Supreme Court junks plea on report will be made public in due course. .Opposition members demanded that the government present the specific facts regarding these "testicular surgeries performed on women". .Rejecting corruption allegations levelled by the BJP against his government, Sukhu said that a contempt motion would soon be brought against the Leader of the Opposition. .In his statement, Thakur, who was the CM when the headline: UNA crowns Allie Grace Broadhead Miss UNA 2027
content: The University of North Alabama has a new Miss UNA, with freshman Allie Grace Broadhead earning the title Saturday night during the university’s annual competition in Florence. Broadhead was crowned Miss UNA 2027 at Norton Auditorium, becoming the 52nd student to hold the title since the tradition began in 1974. She will now represent UNA at the Miss Alabama competition in June 2027. A criminal justice and psychology major, Broadhead performed classical ballet en pointe during the talent portion of the competition. Fourteen contestants competed for the crown, moving through five phases of competition: private interview, onstage question, health and fitness, talent and evening gown. The competition also marked a change in the university’s schedule. UNA moved Miss UNA to the fall this year, giving its winner more time to prepare for the state competition while allowing other contestants additional opportunities to qualify. “By moving Miss UNA to the fall, we hope to give our winner as much time as possible to prepare for Miss Alabama,” said Becca Bush, the event’s organizer and associate director of first-year and retention initiatives.

headline: States' combined fiscal deficit seen narrowing to 2.9% of GDP in FY27
content: States’ combined fiscal deficit, excluding interest-free loans from the Centre for capital expenditure, is budgeted to narrow to 2.9 per cent of GDP in 2026-27 from 3.4 per cent, according to the revised estimates for the previous financial year, a report by PRS Legislative Research released on Tuesday showed. However, nine states have budgeted fiscal deficits exceeding the 3 per cent limit recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, it showed. Including loans under the Centre’s Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI), the combined fiscal deficit is estimated at 3.2 per cent of GDP in 2026-27, compared with 3.8 per cent in the revised estimates for 2025-26, the report said. The scheme provides 50-year interest-free loans to states for capital expenditure. These loans are excluded while calculating the borrowing ceiling. Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Keralam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Punjab, Sikkim and Uttarakhand are among the nine states whose budgeted fiscal deficits exceed the 3 per cent benchmark. Nagaland’s deficit is marginally above the limit at 3.0005 per cent of its gross state domestic product (GSDP). Jammu and Kashmir has the highest budgeted deficit at 3.7 per cent of GSDP, followed by Meghalaya and Himachal Pradesh at about 3.5 per cent each. Manipur, meanwhile, is budgeted to run a fiscal surplus of 0.8 per cent of GSDP, according to data from the report. The report estimated that states would spend ₹68.79 trillion in 2026-27, around 62 per cent more than the Centre’s budgeted expenditure of ₹42.53 trillion. Of the states’ total expenditure, revenue expenditure is estimated at ₹56.36 trillion, while capital expenditure is budgeted at ₹12.43 trillion. Capital expenditure is projected to grow at an annualised rate of 20 per cent between 2024-25 and 2026-27, compared with 13 per cent for revenue expenditure, the report said. The report also flagged the growing fiscal burden of unconditional cash transfers. States have budgeted to spend about ₹4 trillion on such schemes in 2026-27, equivalent to 1 per cent of GDP, compared with 0.6 per cent in 2022-23. “While subsidies can improve access to goods and services, they can also lead to excessive use of subsidised items. Transfers provide direct cash assistance to eligible beneficiaries. They seek to supplement the income of beneficiaries to either buy or produce goods and services, without changing market prices. However, if transfers are not well targeted, they may provide benefits to unintended beneficiaries,” the report said. These transfers cover women, farmers, youth and social security pension beneficiaries, including the elderly, widows and persons with disabilities. The analysis was based on 128 identified schemes and was not an exhaustive estimate, the report said, adding that actual expenditure could be higher. The increase reflects both the introduction of new schemes and higher allocations to existing ones, the report said. Punjab introduced a cash transfer scheme for women in 2026-27, while Keralam and West Bengal increased their allocations towards such schemes. The report noted that states’ revenue expenditure had grown faster than revenue receipts since 2022-23, mainly due to rising subsidies and transfers. The aggregate revenue deficit, which had moderated to 0.23 per cent of GDP in 2022-23, widened to 0.61 per cent in 2024-25 and was estimated at 0.71 per cent in 2025-26. “In 2026-27, transfers to women and social security pensions have the largest share of unconditional cash transfers (UCT). Fourteen states have budgeted to spend more than three-fourths of their total UCT expenditure on social security pension schemes,” it said. Despite states deriving 71 per cent of total GST revenue through SGST collections and the devolution of 41 per cent of CGST, growth in SGST revenue slowed relative to GDP growth in 2025-26 for the first time in four years, the report noted. GST collections, excluding compensation cess, grew 5 per cent during October-March of 2025-26, compared with 9 per cent in April-September, following the GST Council's September 2025 rate rationalisation. The report also noted that the 16th Finance Commission's revised tax devolution formula is set to increase the share of southern and western states such as Karnataka, Keralam, Gujarat and Maharashtra in central tax revenues. This follows the introduction of contribution to national GDP as a new criterion, with a 10 per cent weightage, giving greater allocations to states that account for a larger share of India's economic output. The report also said that states would have spent around ₹33,000 crore under VB-G RAM G in 2025-26, nearly six times the ₹5,261 crore they actually spent under MGNREGA, assuming the same number of person-days and wage rates.

headline: Datanomics: Yamuna's toxic stretch, Delhi pollution 10x above safe limit
content: The Supreme Court has recently warned that states and Union Territories (UTs) in the Yamuna basin will face penalties if water quality deteriorates within their jurisdictions. It comes as Chhath Puja celebrations in Delhi were hit by thick white foam coating the river. Since 2021, at least five of the seven monitoring stations in the national capital have recorded biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of around 30 mg/l during Chhath Puja. This is ten times the prescribed limit of 3 mg/l. BOD measures the oxygen microbes use to break down organic waste; a higher figure indicates greater pollution. Of the four states—Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh—and Delhi through which the river flows, Delhi was the only one in 2025 where every monitoring station exceeded the limit, with a peak reading of 72 mg/l. Pollution typically peaks in summer, when low water flow leaves untreated sewage and industrial effluent barely diluted, and it falls sharply during the monsoon, when excess water dilutes the waste. Last month, Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated Yamuna rejuvenation projects worth over ₹8,941 crore in Delhi.

headline: Andhra Pradesh to get 4 New Universities with ₹3,500 crore investment; 18,000 jobs expected
content: Andhra Pradesh is planning to grow its education system by adding four new university campuses. These new campuses are supported by an estimated investment of ₹3,500 crore. The projects are expected to create a total of 18,000 jobs. Out of these 6,000 jobs will be direct and 12,000 will be indirect. The universities involved in this plan are Global University Systems (GUS) Shoolini University, Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology and Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS). The plan includes two private universities and two off-campus centres of existing deemed-to-be universities. The new campuses are expected to need between 160 and 200 acres of land. Amaravati and Visakhapatnam have been chosen as locations for two of the projects. However, the other two campuses are still looking for locations. Which 4 universities are coming to Andhra Pradesh? The four institutions and their proposed projects are as follows: 1. Global University Systems (GUS), Amaravati: Global University Systems, an international education network. It plans to establish a private university in Amaravati. The project is expected to require around 50 acres of land, which may be provided in two phases. Media reports put the proposed investment at around ₹2,000 crore. The project is expected to generate approximately 1,600 direct and 3,000 indirect jobs. 2. Shoolini University, Andhra Pradesh: Shoolini University of Biotechnology and Management Sciences, based in Solan, Himachal Pradesh, is planning to establish a private university. The proposed investment is around ₹500 crore, with a land requirement of 30 to 50 acres. The project is expected to create around 1,500 direct and 3,000 indirect jobs. However, the state government is yet to finalise its location. 3. Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology, Visakhapatnam: Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology is a deemed-to-be university based in Patiala, Punjab. It plans to establish an off campus centre in Visakhapatnam. The project is expected to involve an investment of around ₹500 crore and require approximately 50 acres of land. It could generate around 1,400 direct and 3,000 indirect jobs. Thapar Institute secured the 26th position in the University category of the NIRF 2025 rankings. 4. NMIMS Off-Campus Centre, Andhra Pradesh: Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS), a deemed-to-be university, is also planning to establish an off-campus centre in Andhra Pradesh. The proposed investment is around ₹500 crore, and the institution may require 30 to 50 acres of land. The project is expected to create approximately 1,500 direct and 3,000 indirect jobs. Its location is yet to be announced. NMIMS secured the 52nd position in the NIRF 2025 University rankings. How much investment and employment will the projects generate? The four projects together are expected to bring an investment of ₹3,500 crore into Andhra Pradesh. The estimated employment impact is as follows: Direct employment: Around 6,000 jobsIndirect employment: Around 12,000 jobsTotal employment: Around 18,000 opportunities Some indirect employment accounted to be from construction, transport, housing, hospitality and other services that support university campuses. These figures are projections linked to the proposed projects. However, the actual investment and job creation will depend on construction, approvals and the development of the campuses. What do the new universities mean for students? The proposed expansion could give students in Andhra Pradesh options for higher education within the state. Students may get access to institutions with established systems and experience in professional education. It could also help reduce the need for some students to move to states, for higher studies. However, the courses offered, admission process, fee structure and academic session details have not yet been announced for the proposed campuses. Regulatory approvals still matter Signing an agreement with the state government does not mean that a university or an off‑campus centre can begin admitting students. The University Grants Commission (UGC) has rules for private universities and for institutions that are deemed to be universities. Under the UGC framework, an institution that is deemed to be a university must obtain the required approvals before it can set up an off‑campus centre. Therefore, the proposed campuses must finish the regulatory and administrative steps before they can start academic operations. The next steps will include finalising land, completing approvals and building the infrastructure. The state government's plan could strengthen education in Andhra Pradesh but the real impact will depend on how fast these projects move from agreements, to operational campuses.

headline: Himachal Government Bans Mandatory Hostel Fees in Medical Colleges, Directs Transparency in Fee Structure
content: The Himachal Pradesh government has issued strict directions to medical colleges across the state to prevent arbitrary fee collection and end the practice of making hostel accommodation compulsory for students. The government has directed all medical colleges affiliated with Atal Medical and Research University (AMRU), Nerchowk, to strictly adhere to the approved fee structure and ensure complete transparency in admission-related charges. In this regard, the Department of Health and Family Welfare has written to the Vice-Chancellor of AMRU, directing the university to ensure uniform implementation of the guidelines across all affiliated institutions. The directions have been issued by Madhu Chaudhary, Special Secretary (Health). As per the directives, all medical colleges must publish their course-wise fee structures, comprising only government-approved charges, on their respective websites. The approved fee details must also be displayed prominently on the AMRU website. Furthermore, complete information regarding fees must be made available to students at the time of declaration of examination results. The government took this step after receiving reports that certain medical colleges were charging students amounts exceeding the prescribed fee structure. There are currently seven medical colleges in Himachal Pradesh, including six government-run institutions and one private institution, Maharishi Markandeshwar Medical College and Hospital, Kumarhatti, Solan. The government has also made it clear that hostel accommodation cannot be imposed as a compulsory condition for admission or continuation of studies. Students will have complete freedom to decide whether they wish to stay in college hostels. Only those opting for hostel facilities will be required to pay the applicable charges as per the approved rates. No student can be compelled, either directly or indirectly, to take hostel accommodation as a condition for securing admission, continuing their studies or appearing in examinations.

The Himachal Pradesh Forest Department has revised its ecological restoration plan for mining-damaged hills in Baddi after the proposed Him-Chandigarh township in Sheetalpur overlapped with land originally identified for rehabilitation. The revised plan shifts the restoration activities away from the affected Sheetalpur area to locations in Dharampur and Nalagarh, while retaining the original financial allocation of INR 1.08 crore. The development follows the state government's approval of the proposed township, which is being planned in the Baddi region of Solan district. According to a report submitted by the Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board (HPSPCB) to the National Green Tribunal (NGT), the Baddi Sub-Divisional Magistrate informed the board in February that the state Cabinet had approved the new township in Sheetalpur. The area overlaps with land identified by the Forest Department for afforestation, retaining structures and check dams to address environmental damage caused by mining. Some of the land identified for restoration had also been transferred to the Himachal Pradesh Housing and Urban Development Authority (HIMUDA), while the diversion of additional land for the township was under consideration. The development led the pollution control board to seek a revised restoration proposal from the Forest Department. The original plan was prepared using environmental compensation of INR 1.08 crore imposed in connection with illegal excavation in the area. It proposed plantation across 37 hectares, construction of 142 check dams, including 118 dry-stone and 24 crate-wire structures, and crate-wire retaining walls at nine locations. The interventions were intended to stabilise soil and restore degraded hill slopes. The revised proposal retains the focus on plantation, soil and moisture conservation and bio-engineering measures. Plantation and staggered contour trenches are planned in Dharampur, while additional trenches are proposed in plantation areas in Nalagarh. Other measures include dry-stone and crate-wire check dams, farm ponds and brushwood check dams along natural drainage channels and gullies. The restoration measures are designed to slow rainwater runoff, reduce soil erosion, trap sediment and improve groundwater recharge. The Forest Department has adopted a ridge-to-valley approach, which involves treating upper catchment areas to help stabilise slopes and reduce the impact of erosion downstream. The plantation component includes indigenous species such as khair, siris, shisham, palash and bamboo. Their root systems are expected to help strengthen soil and improve vegetation cover in degraded areas. The case originated from an application filed by Vijay Chandel before the NGT in 2024, alleging environmental damage linked to illegal excavation. The tribunal had directed the authorities to prepare an action plan for using the environmental compensation towards environmental restoration. HPSPCB has informed the tribunal that the compensation amount would be transferred to the Forest Department for implementing the revised plan, subject to the tribunal's directions. The township-related land changes have therefore required authorities to relocate the restoration activities rather than abandon the proposed rehabilitation work. Source- National Green Tribunal

headline: Himachal Assembly Winter Session: BJP demands probe into corruption during Congress tenure
content: Shimla/Dharamshala (HP), Nov 17 (PTI) Corruption took centre stage on the second day of the Winter Session of the Himachal Pradesh Assembly on Tuesday, as the BJP sought to put the Congress government in the dock on a range of issues, including the ‘smart classroom’ project and the decline in excise revenue. The proceedings saw heated exchanges as Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri intervened to defend the government and his own department. Initiating the debate on the opposition’s adjournment motion, Leader of the Opposition Jai Ram Thakur launched a blistering attack on the government regarding alleged corruption. headline: CM Sukhu releases Sonia Gandhi’s book ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’ in Dharamshala
content: CM Sukhu releases Sonia Gandhi’s book ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’ in Dharamshala Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Monday released the book ” Belonging: A Journey of Love”, authored by senior Congress leader and former UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi, at Dharamshala in Kangra district. The release of the book was attended by members of the state Council of Ministers, senior Congress leaders and other dignitaries, turning the occasion into a prominent political and literary event in the state. Describing the book as a sensitive and insightful account of Sonia Gandhi’s life, Sukhu said it beautifully portrayed her personal journey, struggles and perseverance through challenging circumstances. He said Sonia Gandhi had shaped her life amid numerous difficulties and overcome them with courage, patience and determination. Her journey reflected resilience, strength of character and the ability to adapt to changing circumstances, he added. The Chief Minister said the book offered readers an opportunity to understand Sonia Gandhi’s personal experiences and the challenges she had encountered during different phases of her life. It also carried valuable lessons on confronting difficulties with courage and patience.

headline: Himachal Government Rules Out Regularisation of Special Scheme Teachers
content: The Himachal Pradesh government has ruled out the regularisation of teachers appointed under a special recruitment scheme for government schools, clarifying that there is no proposal or provision to absorb them into regular posts, even after completing two years of service. The Education Minister provided this information in a written reply to a question raised by Dharamshala MLA Sudhir Sharma in the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly. The government’s clarification comes amid thousands of vacant teaching positions in government schools across the state. According to the figures presented in the Assembly, out of 14,987 sanctioned lecturer posts in schools affiliated with the Himachal Pradesh School Education Board, 11,731 are currently filled, leaving 3,256 vacancies. Similarly, in 145 government senior secondary schools affiliated with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), 1,350 out of 2,984 sanctioned lecturer posts are vacant. This brings the total number of vacant lecturer positions across the two categories to 4,606. To address the shortage of teachers in CBSE-affiliated government schools, the state government introduced a special recruitment scheme under which 1,922 teachers have been appointed for fixed tenures. These appointments include 308 English teachers, 305 Mathematics teachers and 154 Commerce teachers, along with teachers in other subjects.

headline: PI-RAHI Signs MoU with Chandigarh Skill Development Mission to Strengthen Healthcare and Industry-Oriented Skills
content: Chandigarh, November 17, 2026: The Chandigarh Skill Development Mission (CSDM), Directorate of Technical Education, Chandigarh Administration, and the PU-IIT Ropar Regional Accelerator for Holistic Innovations Foundation (PI-RAHI) today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen skill development, capacity building, entrepreneurship and innovation in Chandigarh. The MoU was signed by Dr. Palika Arora, PCS, Director, Technical Education-cum-Mission Director, CSDM, Chandigarh Administration, and Prof. (Dr.) Rajat Sandhir, Director, PI-RAHI. The two organisations are already collaborating on the Caregiver Initiative for Chandigarh, including training for Diabetes Care Assistants and geriatric care. The MoU will strengthen this partnership through industry-aligned skilling, upskilling and reskilling programmes, Training of Trainers (ToT), apprenticeships and industrial exposure. The collaboration also envisages developing future-ready skills in Green Hydrogen, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Cybersecurity, Robotics, Drone Technology, the Internet of Things (IoT), Semiconductor Technologies, Electric Vehicles and Industry 4.0. Special emphasis will be placed on promoting women’s entrepreneurship and inclusive skill development, particularly for marginalised communities and economically weaker sections. Both organisations will also explore national and international collaborations, industry partnerships and funding opportunities through government schemes, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives and other agencies to support innovative projects and sustainable livelihoods. The partnership aims to strengthen linkages among academia, industry, government and the innovation ecosystem, contributing to a skilled, entrepreneurial, inclusive and future-ready Chandigarh.

headline: IIT Mandi Research Opens New Possibilities for Next-Gen Memory Devices & Brain-Inspired Computing
content: Mandi, Himachal Pradesh; November 17, 2026: What if imperfections in a material could become its greatest strength? Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Mandi have demonstrated how tiny structural defects in an ultra-thin material can be strategically harnessed to enhance electronic functionality, opening new possibilities for next-generation memory devices and brain-inspired computing. The research, titled “Crack- defect landscapes enable multi modal memristive switching in WS2 mono-bilayers,” explores tungsten disulfide (WS₂), an atomically thin material, for applications in neuromorphic computing – a technology that seeks to replicate the brain's ability to process and store information efficiently. Led by Prof. Viswanath Balakrishnan, along with Anjali Sharma, Yadu Chandran and Bhumit Luhar, the research team studied WS₂-based devices fabricated using chemical vapour deposition (CVD). The researchers investigated how sulphur vacancies (missing atoms) and microscopic cracks influence the movement of electrical charges. A significant finding is that defects traditionally considered manufacturing flaws can be converted into functional features. The interplay between vacancy migration along cracks, resulting in counter-clockwise filamentary switching, and charge trapping and Schottky barrier modulation at the WS₂-metal interface, producing clockwise switching, enables a single planar device to demonstrate multiple switching behaviours. The devices can transition between gradual analog-type conductance changes, abrupt digital switching and low-current, trap-dominated states. This multimodal switching capability could enable a single device architecture to perform functions associated with both artificial synapses and neurons. Biological synapses gradually strengthen or weaken connections, while neurons generate signals when specific thresholds are reached. By emulating these functions, the technology could contribute to future neuromorphic circuits capable of performing computing tasks more efficiently.

headline: Himachal Government Forms 11-Member Panel to Regulate Cannabis Cultivation for Industrial and Medicinal Use
content: Shimla – The Himachal Pradesh government has constituted an 11-member state-level committee to regulate the cultivation of cannabis for non-narcotic purposes and oversee its commercial utilisation for industrial and medicinal applications. Following approval from the Governor, the State Taxes and Excise Department issued a notification in the official gazette on Monday, formally establishing the committee and outlining its responsibilities. The initiative aims to streamline the regulatory framework by bringing various government approvals, from cannabis cultivation to the sale of the produce, under a single-window system. The move is intended to simplify procedures for farmers and industries while ensuring that cultivation and commercial activities remain within the prescribed legal framework. The state-level committee will play a key role in establishing cannabis seed banks and facilitating the supply of quality seeds to farmers. It will also take decisions regarding the procurement of cannabis produce and oversee arrangements for its storage, processing and transportation. In addition, the committee will examine proposals for setting up industrial and medicinal units, determine applicable levies and promote research and development related to non-narcotic cannabis utilisation. The Administrative Secretary of the State Taxes and Excise Department will head the 11-member committee as its chairperson, while the Excise Commissioner will serve as the member-secretary.
